findings.title: `self.downsize` is redefined and overwrites the 5-argument version
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 overwrites the `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method defined right above it on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or 5 arguments with `opts`) will now either pass `max_height` as `opts` (causing a `TypeError`/`NoMethodError` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed on an Integer) or raise an `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` for non-image uploads
findings.body: In `validateUploadedFile`, `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) regardless of `type`. However, the server-side downsizing in `UploadsController` only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. For non-image attachments (`type === 'attachment'`), `max_attachment_size_kb` is no longer enforced on the client: attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` will now be uploaded up to 10MB before being rejected by the server, or attachments > 10MB will be blocked on the client even if an admin configured `max_attachment_size_kb` higher than 10MB.

findings.title: `tempfile.size` may return a cached/stale size or fail to shrink for non-resizable images like SVG
findings.body:
In the downsizing loop:
1. If `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (for example, on an `.svg` file, which `FileHelper.is_image?` treats as an image, or when `gifsicle` fails because `--resize-fit 80%` is not valid gifsicle syntax), `downsize` returns `false`, yet the loop ignores the return value and repeats all 5 attempts pointlessly.
2. `tempfile` is an open `Tempfile`/`File` object; when external `convert` / `ImageOptim` tools rewrite or replace `tempfile.path` on disk (especially if `ImageOptim` replaces the file via atomic rename to a new inode), `tempfile.size` queries the open file descriptor (`fstat`) rather than the path on disk (`File.size(tempfile.path)`), and when `tempfile` is later read in `Upload.create_for` it may read from the old unlinked inode instead of the newly written file at `tempfile.path`.
